promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Oct 18 2026, 2 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Last week went exactly to plan, and that steady base is what you need now. This week trims the volume a little and adds marathon pace miles, and you do not need the 22 miler.

answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer:
No, skip the 22. The 20 miler on Sun Sep 13 and the 17 miler last Sunday already give you the endurance this race needs.

Two weeks out, a 22 would add fatigue faster than it adds fitness, and the tired legs would carry into the taper.

Sunday's 15 miler gives you the same sharpening: 9 easy miles, then 5 miles at marathon pace, then 1 easy mile.

new.analysis:
Last week matched the plan on every day, with no swapped or shortened sessions. The rest days were real rest, and the threshold reps averaged 7:58 per mile without fading. The 17 mile long run ran at 9:59 per mile, and the back half was as fast as the front, which is the even pacing the race needs.

Your easy pace and easy heart rate have barely moved in three weeks, at about 9:50 per mile and 138 to 139 beats per minute. That points to a steady aerobic base, so adding volume now would add fatigue faster than fitness. Moving the race to Oct 18 shortens the build, so the job now is to protect what you already have.

This week starts the taper: about 39 miles, roughly 7 percent less than last week's 42. The quality session shifts from threshold to marathon pace, because the job now is rehearsing race effort rather than building threshold. Sunday keeps 15 miles with only 5 at marathon pace, so you arrive at race week fresh rather than tired.

Use this as your pace guide for the week:

| Effort | Pace per mile | Heart rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy runs | about 9:50 | under 145 |
| Long run easy miles | about 10:00 | under 148 |
| Marathon pace | 8:35 | under 155 |

8:35 per mile is the pace for a 3:45 finish, and the Sunday marathon pace miles are the best check on it. If those miles feel controlled, the goal is realistic. If they feel hard from the first mile, start race day a touch slower rather than forcing the pace.

You told me you feel anxious about the new date, which is a normal response to a moved race. The plan lowers the load gradually, so sleep and truly easy days matter more than any extra miles this week.
